title: The envelope's `source` and `count` are filled, and each is filled where it belongs
scope:
the two envelope fields [0092](0092.md) declared and nothing outside the engine floor
writes — where a record says it was produced, and how a run of identical records is bounded. It
adds no captured call stack, and it changes no part of the record model, which already has both
slots.
dependsOnText:
[0092](0092.md), whose envelope declares `source` and `count`; [0106](0106.md) and
[0020](0020.md), whose floor already coalesces and whose target is already bounded;
[0002](0002.md), whose propagation design is where a call-site constant already reaches the
runtime; [0163](0163.md), whose viewer is the reader that makes the second half worth deciding now.
validatedBy:
the conformance and unit cases the two rules name, landed by the goal that
carries them. Nothing holds this record on its own today, which is why both rules are `designed`.

summary.headline: A log record names the line that produced it, and the file log counts repeats
summary.body:
Every log record carries the file and line it was written from, and an exception's location is
filled in at construction rather than left blank. When the same record repeats in a short
window, the file log target merges the run into one line with a count, because a disk is what a
flood would hurt. The debug stream does not merge: its store groups at read time, so every
occurrence is kept. A per-line rate limit was considered and not taken.
